bib.title: Large Language Models as an Indirect Reasoner: Contrapositive and Contradiction for Automated Reasoning

question: Can prompting LLMs to reason indirectly (contradiction and contrapositive) alongside direct reasoning improve logical reasoning and mathematical proof?
hypothesis: LLMs mostly use direct reasoning; prompting indirect reasoning and voting over both path types enriches reasoning paths and improves accuracy on problems DR cannot solve.
contributions: Introduce the IR strategy (contrapositive and contradiction) into LLM reasoning
Devise prompt templates that stimulate IR and the DIR method combining DR and IR
DIR combines with CoT variants, improving four datasets on three LLMs

method.summary: Prompt templates instruct the LLM to negate the conclusion and derive a contradiction, and to use contrapositives of rules (IR). DIR samples equal numbers of DR and IR chains and takes a majority vote, added on top of SC, CR and MulAD with the same total number of sampled chains.
method.task: logical reasoning (ProofWriter, LogiQA) and mathematical proof (ProofNet, ProofMath)

datasets.name: LogiQA
datasets.split: questions with minimal dependence on external sources

datasets.name: ProofWriter (OWA, 5-hop subset)
datasets.source: Tafjord et al., 2021; sampling after Kazemi et al., 2023

datasets.name: ProofMath
datasets.source: new; junior/senior high school textbooks and zuoyebang.com; proofs verified by three experts
datasets.preprocessing: Table 7 distribution: junior algebra 6+11, geometry 7+8+8; high school algebra 13+19+12, geometry 7+9

datasets.name: ProofWriter_S
datasets.split: selected subset of ProofWriter to showcase IR

inference.decoding: sampling M reasoning chains, majority vote over answers (Eq. 5)
inference.temperature: 0.7 GPT-3.5-turbo, 0.9 Gemini-pro, 0.6 Llama-3-70B; CR intermediate thoughts 0.1, 0.3, 0.3 respectively
inference.samples: 16 chains for LogiQA and ProofWriter, 4 for ProofNet and ProofMath, equal split DR/IR in DIR; 4 chains for the DR vs IR comparison (Tables 5, 6); same total as baseline
inference.prompting: few-shot with worked examples (IR examples show contradiction/contrapositive); zero-shot variant with instructions only (Table 6)

other.preliminary experiment: 70 questions from each of 4 datasets prompted with 'Let's think step by step' to count DR vs IR share (Fig 3, values not in text)

metrics.name: AA (accuracy of answer)
metrics.definition: AN/N, share of examples with correct answer

metrics.name: AP (accuracy of reasoning process)
metrics.definition: PN/N, share with correct reasoning process; judged by humans

metrics.name: DP (diversity of reasoning processes)
metrics.definition: (1/N) sum d_i, d_i = number of correct reasoning methods for example i

eval.protocol: Single table values, no seeds or significance tests stated. LogiQA scored by AA; ProofWriter scored by AA (Table 2 caption says accuracy); proofs scored by 5 graduate students (3 CS, 2 math), blind to method, shuffled, majority vote of independent judgments.

availability.data: ProofMath described (Appendix B.2); release not stated

prompts.text: First, take the negation of the conclusion/question and assume the negation is true; Next, use the negation and the premises to deduce its falsity until the result of that assumption is a contradiction. If necessary, consider the logical equivalence of the original rules and their contrapositive.

prompts.purpose: IR template for CoT on ProofWriter (system part)
prompts.text: Suppose you are one of the greatest AI scientists, logicians and mathematicians. Let's think about it step by step. You need to use proof by contradiction to judge whether the following conclusion is True, False or Unknown. First, take the negation of the conclusion and assume the negation to be true or false in turn. Then, use the premises and rules to deduce whether the assumption leads to a contradiction. If a contradiction arises, the assumption is false. If not, the assumption cannot be determined. If necessary, consider the logical equivalence of the original rules and their contrapositive.
prompts.where: Appendix E, Fig 12 (also Figs 13-19 for CR, LogiQA, ProofNet, ProofMath)

results.claim: On LogiQA with GPT-3.5-turbo, SC-DIR beats SC by 7.2 points.
results.table: Table 1, row SC-DIR vs SC, GPT-3.5-turbo

results.claim: On ProofWriter, MulAD-DIR with Llama-3-70B reaches 87.5% vs 78.0% for MulAD.
On Gemini-pro ProofWriter, SC-DIR is 57.0% vs SC 46.0%, above 10 points gain.
On ProofWriter_S with GPT-3.5-turbo, IR alone gets 50.7% vs 17.3% for DR, a 33.4 point gain.
results.setup: ProofWriter_S 150 hand-selected items, SC with 4 chains, few-shot
results.table: Table 5, row ProofWriter_S IR, column GPT-3.5-turbo
results.note: Subset was chosen by authors to showcase IR, so the gap is not representative of the full dataset.

results.claim: On ProofMath_S with GPT-3.5-turbo, IR gets 82.6% vs 57.1% for DR (25.5 points).
results.setup: ProofMath_S 35 hand-selected items, SC with 4 chains
results.table: Table 5, row ProofMath_S IR, column GPT-3.5-turbo
results.note: 82.6% is not a multiple of 1/35 (29/35=82.9%); printed as is.

results.claim: Zero-shot IR prompts (instructions only) still beat DR: ProofWriter_S GPT-3.5-turbo 49.3% vs 15.3%.
results.table: Table 6, row ProofWriter_S IR, column GPT-3.5-turbo

results.claim: On ProofNet, SC-DIR raises process accuracy and diversity over SC with GPT-3.5-turbo.
results.table: Table 3, row SC-DIR, column GPT-3.5-turbo AP

results.claim: On ProofMath, CR-DIR raises AP over CR by 15 points with GPT-3.5-turbo (72.0 vs 57.0).
results.table: Table 4, row CR-DIR, column GPT-3.5-turbo AP
results.note: Text: 10.0% AP enhancement, rising to 15.0% with GPT-3.5-turbo.

results.claim: Removing either contrapositive or contradiction instructions from IR degrades IR on ProofWriter_S.
results.note: Values only in Fig 5, not in text.

results.claim: Without prompting, LLMs rarely use IR on logical reasoning tasks.
results.setup: 70 questions from each of four datasets, 'Let's think step by step'

limits: Authors concede gains vary by model: GPT-3.5-turbo performs IR more effectively and stably than Gemini-pro.
Only contrapositive and contradiction explored; other logical laws left to future work.
Test sets are small (50 to 200 items), single runs, no significance tests or seeds reported.
DR vs IR comparison uses authors' hand-selected subsets (ProofWriter_S, ProofMath_S) chosen to showcase IR.
Proof correctness judged by 5 graduate students; model versions and dates not given; GPT-3.5, Gemini-pro and Llama-3-70B are dated.

contrapositive and contradiction, logically equivalent to DR
Direct-Indirect Reasoning: DR and IR as parallel reasoning paths merged by voting
